what: Mahabodhi dispute: Mahabodhi Society (founded Ceylon 1891) sought possession of the temple for Buddhists; 1893 attempt to obtain lease/conveyance from the Mahanth failed; Government said it could not further the Society's objects but there was freedom of worship.
quote: 1893 an endeavour was made on behalf of the Society to obtain a lease or conveyance of the temple from the Mahanth of Bodh Gaya

what: 1896: the Society's Secretary placed a Buddha image in the temple without permission; the Mahanth's disciples resented it, a disturbance followed, the image was removed and the persons expelled; criminal prosecution convicted some disciples in local courts, acquitted by the High Court (s.296 IPC).
quote: Tins action was resented by the disciples of the Mahanth, and a disturbance ensued which resulted in the removal of the image

what: High Court finding: the Mahanth was in possession, sole superintendent of the temple and took all offerings of both Hindus and Buddhists; yet the temple, though in Hindu Mahanths' possession, was never converted into a Hindu temple, Buddhists having free access; since July 1894 the Mahanth and disciples carried on 'a sort of spurious Hindu worship' of the Buddha image.
quote: the Malaanth was in possession, was sole superintendent of the tempde, and took all the offerings both of Hindus and Buddhists.

what: Gazetteer's judgment: the temple, originally Buddhist, long in the hands of a Hindu Mahanth 'belonging to an order founded by one of the bitterest enemies of Buddhism' (Sankara); Government restored it at its own cost; the Mahanth keeps asserting his authority and control of worship.
